name: EXACT_CHANNEL_DECOMPOSITION_APPLICATION_CONTRACT

epistemic_firewall.structural_statement: The abstract two-block theorem is mathematically valid whenever its hypotheses hold.
epistemic_firewall.application_statement: Using it algorithmically on a new graph additionally requires a graph-only decomposition certificate and polynomially checkable application receipts.
epistemic_firewall.forbidden_inference: A valid theorem does not imply that discovering a suitable decomposition in an arbitrary input graph is polynomial.

required_fields: anchors c in L and f in R
port sets P_L subseteq L\{c}, P_R subseteq R\{f}
exact channel graph X=E(L,R) subseteq P_L x P_R
exact_interface_checks: Partition is total and pairwise disjoint.
Every L-R edge belongs to X.
Every X-edge has one endpoint in P_L and one in P_R.
No L-R edge exists outside X.
object_certificate.verification_complexity: Polynomial in |V|+|E| for a supplied decomposition certificate.

canonical_positive_output.solution_family: All implication-successor-closed R with R_min subseteq R subseteq R_max.

DECOMPOSITION_DISCOVERABLE.compact_negative_output: A directed implication path r0 -> ... -> ell0 with r0 in R0 and ell0 in L0.
DECOMPOSITION_DISCOVERABLE.semantic_firewall: The polynomial reachability result applies to the pure abstract exact-channel interface only. Extra future C11/source-role/semantic restrictions require separate analysis.

procedure: Construct the bipartite channel graph X.
Compute k=nu(X) by exact bipartite maximum matching.
Preserve one maximum matching M of size k.
Preserve one minimum vertex cover U of X and verify |U|=k.
Use the abstract local theorem to conclude lambda_G(c,f)=k+1.
LOCAL_FORMULA_CERTIFIED.polynomiality: Bipartite matching and verification of M/U are polynomial.
LOCAL_FORMULA_CERTIFIED.exact_upper_cut: {z} union U is an explicit c-f separator of size k+1.

LOCAL_TO_GLOBAL_TRANSFER_CERTIFIED.meaning: Whether the equality kappa(G)=lambda_G(c,f)=1+nu(X) has been certified.

structural_route.label: STRUCTURAL_AUTHORITY
mechanism: For every S with |S|<=k consider the component-refined quotient hat_B_S whose vertices are connected components of G[L-S], connected components of G[R-S], and surviving {z}.
If hat_B_S is connected for every such S, the abstract component-refined theorem gives kappa(G)>=k+1.
Together with the explicit cut {z} union U, conclude kappa(G)=lambda_G(c,f)=k+1.
structural_route.complexity_warning: Literal enumeration of all S with |S|<=k is not polynomial when k is unbounded; this route is not automatically an efficient recognition algorithm.

algorithmic_route.label: ALGORITHMIC_CERTIFICATION
procedure: Verify the supplied exact-channel decomposition graph-only.
Layer 1 immediately certifies lambda_G(c,f)=k+1 and gives kappa(G)<=k+1 via {z} union a minimum vertex cover.
Independently compute/certify the exact global vertex connectivity kappa(G) with a polynomial vertex-connectivity / minimum-vertex-cut algorithm.
If the certified value satisfies kappa(G)>=k+1, the previous upper bound forces kappa(G)=k+1=lambda_G(c,f).
algorithmic_route.equivalent_test: Because the abstract local theorem always gives kappa(G)<=k+1, transfer equality holds iff kappa(G)>=k+1, equivalently iff kappa(G)=k+1.
algorithmic_route.role: Polynomial recognition/certification of transfer once a decomposition certificate is available.
algorithmic_route.explanation_limit: This route certifies equality but does not by itself explain which structural mechanism makes every refined interface quotient robust.

equivalent_transfer_conditions: G-S is connected for every S subseteq V(G) with |S|<=k
hat_B_S is connected for every S with |S|<=k
exact_characterization.qualification: Use the standard non-small finite-graph convention in which vertex connectivity is the minimum size of a vertex set whose deletion disconnects the graph or leaves the applicable trivial case.

recognition_vs_certification.decomposition_discovery: Polynomial for the pure exact-channel interface by canonical implication reachability. Generic 2-SAT is not needed: fixed-triple feasibility is a closure/reachability test.
recognition_vs_certification.local_formula_certification: Polynomial after graph-only discovery or a supplied valid decomposition.
recognition_vs_certification.local_to_global_equality_certification: Polynomial after discovery/supply of the decomposition, by bipartite matching plus exact vertex-connectivity computation.
recognition_vs_certification.structural_mechanism_classification: Separate explanatory task; examples include block robustness, component-refined external reconnection, hub redundancy, matching/cover geometry, or another proved mechanism.
recognition_vs_certification.canonical_solution_structure: For each feasible fixed triple, R_min and R_max are canonical extremal decompositions, and all feasible R-sides form a distributive lattice of implication-upsets between them.
recognition_vs_certification.negative_certificate: A forced-R to forced-L implication path is a compact proof-carrying NO-DECOMPOSITION certificate for a fixed triple.

phase_A_exact_channel_decomposition_disc.question: Which authoritative C11 residuals satisfy the pure exact-channel interface, and which additional C11 role restrictions are required?
fixed_triple_receipt: either R_min=Reach(R0) disjoint from L0, or a path R0 -> L0

phase_B_transfer_mechanism_classificatio.question: For discovered decompositions with certified equality kappa=lambda=1+nu(X), what structural mechanism explains the transfer?

discovery.negative: directed path r0 -> ... -> ell0, r0 in R0, ell0 in L0

easy_application_corollary.name: CANONICAL_REACHABILITY_DISCOVERY_AND_POLYNOMIAL_TRANSFER_CERTIFICATION
easy_application_corollary.statement: For the pure exact-channel interface, graph-only discovery is polynomial by implication reachability. The algorithm can output a canonical minimal-R decomposition, canonical maximal-R bound, or a compact forced-R-to-forced-L path certificate. Once a decomposition is found, local formula and local-to-global transfer equality are polynomially certifiable by matching/cover and exact vertex connectivity.
easy_application_corollary.caveat: Stronger future C11 semantic restrictions are not automatically covered.

next_action: No new scientific gate. Future applications should use canonical reachability discovery first, then separately audit additional C11 semantic restrictions and local-to-global transfer mechanism.

prior_2SAT_discovery.relation: Still correct; superseded as the sharp fixed-triple normal form by directed reachability.
